summary_en: Marks a stretch of time: how long something lasted, or the span during which something else happened.
ja_diff_note: 동안 covers both 間 (during) and the duration suffix 〜間 (三日間 = 3일 동안). After a verb it always takes -는, even for past events (자는 동안 = 寝ている間), and it never marks a single point in time -- that is 때.
notes: Noun + 동안: 방학 동안, 일주일 동안, 두 시간 동안 (= 二時間).
Verb stem + -는 동안 = while: 엄마가 요리하는 동안. Keep -는 even in the past: 제가 자는 동안 비가 왔어요.
동안 = a span; 때 = a point or occasion (어렸을 때); 중 = in the middle of an activity (회의 중).
오랫동안 (for a long time) is written as one word.

examples.ko: 서울에 있는 동안 할머니 댁에서 지냈어요.
examples.en: While I was in Seoul, I stayed at Grandma's place.
examples.ja: ソウルにいる間、おばあちゃんの家で過ごしました。

examples.ko: 나 샤워하는 동안 밥 좀 해 줘.
examples.en: Make some rice while I shower, would you?
examples.ja: 私がシャワーしてる間、ご飯炊いといて。

drills.explain_en: A length of time takes 동안 (二時間待った); 때 marks a point, and 까지 needs an end point, not a length.

drills.prompt_ko: 아빠가 텃밭에서 일하는 ___ 엄마는 김밥을 만들었어요.
drills.prompt_en: While Dad worked in the garden, Mom made gimbap.
drills.explain_en: -는 + 동안 means 'while'; 전에 needs -기 전에 and 때문에 needs -기 때문에.

drills.prompt_en: While Seoyun was showering, I did the dishes.
drills.explain_en: 동안 always takes the -는 form, even when the whole sentence is in the past.

drills.prompt_en: When I was little, I lived in Japan.
drills.explain_en: -았/었을 때 is the fixed 'when (I was)' pattern; 동안 would need -는, and 중 attaches to action nouns.
